core_goal: Incorporate limited aromatic units into an aliphatic polyester backbone to enhance rigidity while maintaining hydrolytic degradation sites.
mechanism_one_liner: Aromatic monomers increase chain rigidity and glass transition temperature, improving heat resistance
risk_one_liner: Aromatic content may reduce enzymatic degradation efficiency
pros_short: Directly increases Tg and rigidity via aromatic units
cons_short: Aromatic content can significantly slow enzymatic hydrolysis
Phase separation risk may complicate processing and properties

core_goal: Introduce acid/ester-containing crosslinkers that reinforce thermal stability but cleave under environmental conditions.
mechanism_one_liner: Crosslinks restrict chain mobility at high temperatures but contain strategically positioned ester bonds
pros_short: Crosslinking effectively restricts chain mobility for thermal stability
Cleavable crosslinks designed to fragment first, enabling degradation
cons_short: Precise control of crosslink density and distribution is challenging
Risk of premature hydrolysis during processing or storage

core_goal: Integrate bicyclic monomers that elevate Tg while maintaining hydrolysable backbone linkages.
mechanism_one_liner: Fused ring structures introduce kinetic barriers to chain rotation, increasing thermal stability without strong intermolecular interactions that slow degradation
pros_short: Bio-derived rigid monomers like isosorbide are commercially available
Increases Tg through chain stiffness without strong crystallinity
cons_short: May lead to brittleness and processing difficulties at high loadings
Polymerization kinetics can be slower with bulky monomers
